title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
goal: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
steps: 1. Name — Name five versions of the task from almost easy to genuinely stretching. Effort Staircase — breathe naturally.
2. Cross Out — Remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Remain Version — Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed. Effort Staircase — pick action.
4. Climb Stair — Next time, climb only one stair. Effort Staircase — next action.

title: TWO ENGINES
goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
steps: 1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence. Two Engines — loosen hands.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only. Two Engines — pick action.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything. Two Engines — next action.

5. Learning — Learning happens in the missed appointment. Let Urge — next action.

title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
steps: 1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body. Ride Craving — widen gaze.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, Imagine the next point without acting on the urge. Ride Craving — name feeling.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour. Ride Craving — next action.

3. End Completely — When it ends, stop completely, feel the after-pulse, and drink water. Burn Excess — name sensation.
4. Let Body — Let the body spend energy without spending your future. Burn Excess — next action.

title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.
steps: 1. Breathe Pulling — Breathe in without pulling extra air. Longer Out — move slowly.
2. Let Outflow — Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
3. Repeat Comfortable — Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose. Longer Out — pick action.
4. Breathe Workable — After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision. Longer Out — next action.

title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
goal: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.
steps: 1. Smallest — Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach. Turn Up — soften shoulders.
2. Pause Enlarge — Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Ask Whether — Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing. Turn Up — notice detail.
4. Let Determine — Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop. Turn Up — next action.

title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
goal: Duty becomes clearer after fear and praise exit the room.
steps: 1. Name Role — Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it. Remains Reward — widen gaze.

3. Ask Responsibility — Ask which responsibility still stands. Remains Reward — split duty.
4. Set Role Limit — Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require. Remains Reward — next action.

3. End Hands — When time ends, open hands, name the boundary underneath, and select a safe action. Anger Walls — next action.

title: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
goal: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
steps: 1. Count Usable — Count the usable work blocks remaining, subtracting sleep and fixed duties. Break Deadline — breathe naturally.
2. Give Block — Give each block one deliverable with a visible finish.
3. Place Buffers — Place buffers before the final deadline. Break Deadline — pick action.
4. Start Earliest — Start the earliest window; refuse to mentally carry later windows inside it. Break Deadline — next action.

title: RUN THE TWO-WORD TASK
goal: Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.
steps: 1. Scan Work — Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check. Run Two — move slowly.
2. Pick Verb — Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
3. Bind Object — Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now. Run Two — notice detail.
4. Run Command — Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object genuinely needs to change. Run Two — next action.

title: THE EMOTION STOPS AT THE SKIN
goal: Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.
steps: 1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body. Emotion Stops — breathe naturally.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership. Emotion Stops — split duty.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred. Emotion Stops — next action.

title: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
goal: Find the choice that survives without witnesses.
steps: 1. Imagine Nobody — Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action. Remove Audience — soften shoulders.
2. Erase Audience — Erase the imagined audience one row at a time.
3. Choose Direct — What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained?. Remove Audience — split duty.
4. Take Smallest — Take the smallest version privately. Remove Audience — next action.

steps: 1. Place Memory — Place the memory on a screen with enough visual distance. Move Memory — breathe naturally.
2. View Scene — View the scene from above, behind, or beside a compassionate observer.
3. Keep Events — Keep events accurate while changing camera position. Move Memory — notice detail.
4. Add Resources — Add current-you outside the frame with present resources. Move Memory — next action.

title: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
goal: The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.
steps: 1. Headline Event — State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay. Ask Memory — breathe naturally.
2. Extract Claim — Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route Bill — Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category. Ask Memory — notice detail.
4. Act Present — Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide. Ask Memory — next action.

title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
goal: Empathy does not sign their conclusion.
steps: 1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it. Understand Disagree — breathe naturally.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs. Understand Disagree — notice detail.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence. Understand Disagree — next action.

title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
goal: Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.
steps: 1. Issue Recurring — Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately. Fight Three — loosen hands.
2. Give Own — Give each its own conclusion and action. Fight Three — name event.
3. Don't Erase — Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context. Fight Three — next action.

title: BURY THE GOAL, FREE THE ENERGY
goal: Some ambitions deserve a formal ending.
steps: 1. Name Goal — Name the goal, why it once mattered, what changed, and which obligations can now close. Bury Goal — hear sound.
2. Keep Value — Thank any value it revealed. Bury Goal — notice detail.
3. Cancel — Cancel one concrete commitment, archive materials, and redirect the recovered resource toward a living priority. Bury Goal — next action.

goal: Separate existence from likelihood and support.
steps: 1. State Lines — State three lines: It is possible that…; It is probable that…; The evidence currently supports…. Possible Probable — move slowly.

3. Plan Probability — Base planning on probability and safety margin, not possibility alone. Possible Probable — next action.

title: THIS IS A CHAPTER, NOT THE BOOK
goal: The present cannot forecast unopened pages.
steps: 1. Place Today — Position today’s event on a long timeline with past chapters already survived and blank space ahead. Chapter Book — move slowly.
2. Picture Future — Picture three future signposts that remain possible but unknown. Chapter Book — allow opposite.
3. Choose Sentence — Choose one sentence describing this chapter accurately without making it the title of the whole life. Chapter Book — next action.

title: THOUGHTS MUST BRING AN AGENDA
goal: Extended thinking is earned by a clear question and output.
steps: 1. Give Topic — Before giving a topic more time, require two items: the exact question and the form of a useful result—decision, plan, explanation, message, or acceptance. Thoughts Must — loosen hands.

3. Ground — Ground through ordinary action immediately afterward. Let Watcher — next action.
